issues.description: The problem statement's UML and description expect Stock to provide an emptyStock() method, but the template Stock implementation declares clearInventory() instead. The solution uses emptyStock(). This name/signature mismatch between the problem statement, template, and solution can confuse students about which method they should call and may prevent them from implementing or testing behavior that relies on emptyStock().
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method name across artifacts. Either rename the template's clearInventory() method to emptyStock(), or update the problem statement and solution to refer to clearInventory(). Ensure the method signature (public void emptyStock()/clearInventory()) is consistent in template and solution and matches the UML/specification.

issues.description: The operation for clearing the stock inventory is named inconsistently: the problem statement (UML) declares emptyStock(), the solution implements emptyStock(), but the template Stock class provides clearInventory(). This mismatch can confuse students about the expected method name when mapping requirements to the provided code and the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the problem statement and solution by renaming clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or add a delegating emptyStock() method that calls clearInventory(). This ensures a single, consistent method name for clearing the stock across all artifacts.
